notes: Source side is the activity_report.json user_activity_daily.py itself wrote to S3 for the pinned day, split into four bronze tables by databricks/migration/p3/recon/load_legacy_baseline_user_activity.py; target side is the four gold tables the converted job writes. The legacy ships one JSON document, so the split is the only way this reconciles as rows rather than as bytes. Four objects because the legacy's blob has four grains: the trends block, the daily_summaries array, the user_summaries array, and the actions_by_type map inside each user summary. top_users is NOT a fifth object: it is user_summaries[:20] and the loader refuses a baseline where the two disagree, so a target that ranks differently cannot pass one comparison and fail the other. generated_at is not mapped, being a wall clock. The two windows are deliberately different widths (31 dates of summary rows, 30 dates of top-user objects, C-3.1/C-3.2) and the report is written for one report_date, so both sides are scoped to it rather than compared across days. user_id carries the literal 'unknown' (C-2.7) and action_type the literal 'NaN' and the unnormalised dotted 'document.created' (F-0.9); those are values to match, not defects to clean up. rank is a compared field and not part of any key, so a target that computes the right numbers in the wrong order is a mismatch on rank instead of a silently re-joined pass. avg_daily_events is the only float: Python round() is half-to-even, so the target computes it with bround(), and the 1e-9 relative tolerance applies on top of that.
